Keysight B1500A/B1505A/B1506A/B1507A Device Analyzer Series Programming Guide, Edition 15, May 2022: PG p433 (4-115)

=== PG p433 (4-115) · Programming Guide > 4 Command Reference > Command Reference > ERSSP ===
Keysight B1500 Series Programming Guide, Edition 15 4-115
Command Reference
ERSSP
Example
Statements
OUTPUT @B1500;"ERS?"
ENTER @B1500;A
PRINT "Port Status=";A
For example, 255 (0000000011111111) is returned when the port 0 to 7 have
been set to the TTL low level and the port 8 to 15 have been set to the TTL high
level.
See Also “ERMOD”, “ERC”, “ERM”
ERSSP
This command sets the connection state of the I/O path for the Keysight 16440A
SMU/PGU selector (B1500A-A04). Set it for each output port on the selector.
Execution
Conditions
Digital I/O port must be set to the 16440A control mode using the ERMOD 1
command.
Syntax ERSSP port,status
Parameters port: Output port of SMU/PG selector. Integer expression.
0: Output 1 on the first selector
1: Output 2 on the first selector
2: Output 1 on the second selector
3: Output 2 on the second selector
status: Connection status of I/O path. Integer expression.
0: All open. Breaks connection. Initial setting.
1: SMU on. Makes connection to the SMU input.
2: PGU on. Makes connection to the PGU input.
3: PGU open. Open status made by opening the semiconductor relay
installed on the PGU on path.
Example
Statements
OUTPUT @B1500;"ERMOD 1"
OUTPUT @B1500;"ERSSP 0,2"
See Also “ERMOD”
Keysight B1500A/B1505A/B1506A/B1507A Device Analyzer Series Programming Guide, Edition 15, May 2022: PG p154 (2-66)

=== PG p154 (2-66) · Programming Guide > 2 Remote Mode Functions > SMU/PG Selector ===
2-66 Keysight B1500 Series Programming Guide, Edition 15
Remote Mode Functions
SMU/PG Selector
SMU/PG Selector
The Keysight 16440A SMU/PGU Selector (B1500A-A04) is used to switch the
measurement resources connected to DUT (device under test). The Input ports must
be connected to the measurement resources, an SMU and an SPGU or others, and
the Output port must be connected to the DUT interface. For the SMU connection,
connect the Force terminal only. The Sense terminal must be open.
Use the ERMOD and ERSSP commands to control the 16440A selector. The
ERMOD command sets the Digital IO control mode. The ERSSP command sets the
selector channel CH 1 or CH 2 input-output path to the SMU connect, PGU connect,
or open (no connection).
Figure 2-39 SMU/PG Selector Block Diagram and Connections
The selector CH 1 additionally provides the PGU open status which is made by
keeping the PGU side mechanical relay close and opening the semiconductor relay.
This is effective for applications requiring frequent PGU open/connect switching
because a semiconductor relay is durable compared to a mechanical relay.
The B1500A can use up to two selectors by connecting the selector control cable
between the CONTROL Output connector of the first selector and the CONTROL
Input connector of the second selector.

=== SEL p12 (6) · User's Guide > Operation ===
6 Keysight 16440A User’s Guide, Edition 6
User's Guide
Operation
• Switching state
The switching state of a channel is indicated by the green LEDs on the selector
front panel. This table shows the relation of the relays and the LEDs for each
switching state.
The “PGU open” state is useful if a lot of switching needs to be performed.
When the switching state changes from “PGU on” to “PGU open”, only the
semiconductor relay switches. This reduces the amount of times the mechanical
relay is switched. The semiconductor relay has a much longer switching life than
the mechanical relay.

content.text:
`ERSSP <port>,3` puts one output of the Keysight 16440A SMU/PGU selector into the **"PGU open"** state. The PGU (pulse generator) is disconnected from that output by opening only the semiconductor relay; the mechanical relay on the PGU path stays closed.

**From the manual**

- **Command reference**, PG p433 (4-115): `ERSSP port,status` sets the connection state of each selector output. The status values are:
  - `0`: all open (the initial setting)
  - `1`: SMU on
  - `2`: PGU on
  - `3`: PGU open, "made by opening the semiconductor relay installed on the PGU on path"

  You must first switch the digital I/O port to 16440A control mode with `ERMOD 1`.
- **Why it exists**, PG p154 (2-66) and SEL p12 (6): it's for applications that switch the PGU on and off many times. Going from PGU on (2) to PGU open (3) only flips the semiconductor relay, which lasts much longer than the mechanical relay. The 16440A guide says it "reduces the amount of times the mechanical relay is switched."
- **Which outputs support it**, PG p154 (2-66) and SEL p27 (21): only selector **CH 1** has the PGU-open state. In `ERSSP` port numbers, that's ports `0` and `2` (Output 1 on the first and second selector). The ERSSP command page doesn't say this itself, so don't count on status 3 working on ports `1` or `3`.
- **Reading it back**, PG p434 (4-116): `ERSSP? port` returns `3` when that output is in PGU open.

In this project the selector is controlled through the `b1500` tools and recipes. You can't send `ERSSP` as a raw command.
